title: Cache Stampede and Hot-Key Problems knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which approach best captures the central idea of “Cache Stampede and Hot-Key Problems”?
options: Cache Stampede and Hot-Key Problems should be applied by naming the data, stating assumptions, checking command semantics, and testing a relevant boundary case.
Assume Redis makes every multi-command business workflow automatically durable and rollback-safe.
Skip compatibility checks because every Redis service has identical commands.
Use production customer data for the first experiment.
questions.answer_key: Cache Stampede and Hot-Key Problems should be applied by naming the data, stating assumptions, checking command semantics, and testing a relevant boundary case.
questions.explanation: The lesson is about Cache Stampede and Hot-Key Problems. State assumptions and verify the behavior that Redis and the application each guarantee; the other choices overstate guarantees or create avoidable risk.

questions.prompt: What is the most dependable way to practice “Cache Stampede and Hot-Key Problems”?
options: Start with a minimal synthetic example, predict the result, run an appropriate check, and test one edge case.
Change multiple unrelated settings at once and rely on one successful run.
Ignore the server version, return values, and error behavior.
Treat a static code preview as proof the Redis command executed.
questions.answer_key: Start with a minimal synthetic example, predict the result, run an appropriate check, and test one edge case.
questions.explanation: Small, reproducible examples and explicit checks make expected behavior and limitations easier to understand.

questions.prompt: Before using the technique from “Cache Stampede and Hot-Key Problems” in a real service, what should be confirmed?
options: Its command semantics, version/provider support, security boundary, and failure/recovery behavior relevant to the workload.
Only that the key name is short.
That the operation never needs monitoring or error handling.
That Redis replaces the primary database by default.
questions.answer_key: Its command semantics, version/provider support, security boundary, and failure/recovery behavior relevant to the workload.
questions.explanation: Redis behavior, optional capabilities, operational guarantees and provider support must be checked for the actual deployment.
